newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA'S ACCLAIM TO LIST AS PURE URANIUM PLAY.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA'S ACCLAIM TO LIST AS PURE URANIUM PLAY.

text.p: Acclaim Uranium NL, Australia's first uranium float in more than 20 years, planned to list on the Australian Stock Exchange on September 30, managing director Malcolm Mason said on Thursday.

Acclaim's emergence as a potential uranium producer follows the Australian government's ending of the previous Labor government's "three mines" policy last year and comes as part of an industry swing in interest back toward uranium.
The Perth-based explorer has now lodged a prospectus with the Australian Securities Commission for the issue of 25 million 20 cent shares, underwritten by Morgan Corporate Ltd.
Mason, on a roadshow ahead of the listing, told Reuters the birth of Acclaim Uranium was the result of the company recognising a window in the world uranium market.

Working from a database issued by the Western Australian Department of Mines of uranium discoveries in the state, Acclaim put together a portfolio of 15 of the top 20 uranium deposits in the state, covering a total area of 5,824 sq km, he said.

The holdings do not yet encompass a proven mineable deposit but several possible early production targets exist in the portfolio and it plans to spend at least A$3.15 million over the next two years on exploration, Acclaim said in its prospectus.
A widening uranium shortfall was looming, with surplus inventories of uranium oxide (U3O8) to be depleted by 1999, it said.
World power reactors now required 72,000 tonnes of U3O8 a year, while mines supplied only 42,000 tonnes, Acclaim said.
Electricity demand by 2020 was expected to be at least 50 percent higher than current levels, the prospectus said.
Uranium now accounted for 17 percent of world energy generation, while Southeast Asian power production was a major growth area.
Market fundamentals for uranium were very good, Mason said.
Australia had more than 30 percent of the world's known uranium resources but produced only 11 percent of supplies, he said.

Acclaim's prospectus said that, based on a report by independent geologist Snowden Mining Industry Consultants, it has an estimated 2,728 tonnes of uranium oxide in the ground in 5.2 million tonnes of ore at an average grade of 0.52 kg of U3O8 per tonne.
On listing, Acclaim will be one of two pure uranium companies in Australia.
The other is the leading uranium producer, Energy Resources of Australia Ltd, which mines in the Northern Territory in the South Alligator River region.
Australia's other main existing producer is WMC Ltd, which produces uranium as a major by-product in its Olympic Dam copper mine in South Australia.
One of Acclaim's prospects, Kintyre East, is next to Rio Tinto Plc/Ltd's major deposit at Kintyre, which is planned to be in production in about two years' time.
